The most interesting thing about social trading is that for the first time in years, there’s actual alpha to find on the timeline again.

I’ve come across several calls over the last few weeks that did a clean 5-10x right after, with enough time and liquidity to actually accumulate.

Haven’t felt this since 2019, back before the whole thing turned into an insider game where the moment you saw something on the timeline, you were already exit liquidity.

Feels good to see people winning together again, instead of the endless PvP where it was just about extracting each other.

Never stop scrolling.

New Borrow Rate For USDe

Aave's USDe reserve inherited the USDC curve, built for assets that pay holders nothing. So a supplier earned 1.83% on a token worth 4.80% staked, and cheap debt against higher-paying collateral turned into a 10x loop.

The new rate tracks what USDe itself pays. At full implementation the max-leverage position goes from 23.1% to negative.

The Primitive Underneath Credit

Every variable rate has to vary against something, which means every DeFi lending rate you've ever taken came out of a model someone picked for you.

This article starts one level lower, with a zero-coupon obligation: a borrower promises $100 in a year, a lender offers $95 today, and the market decides what the promise is worth. The rate falls out of the price.

Crypto has the most insane rags-to-riches stories

Few things have minted more new millionaires on the internet. More than YouTube, more than any single company. That’s a big reason the whole space commands attention

No better way to build a brand than making your followers rich

Someone will say it’s also created so much value destruction. Markets are volatile, but this asset class went from zero to ~$3T, distributed across millions of people

Love it or hate it, crypto will keep capturing more mindshare.

tweets.text:
David Sacks: Trump’s Instincts on AI and Data Centers Are Right

@Jason:

“Trump is going to turn out to be right about this data center issue.”

@DavidSacks:

“I have told you guys before that Trump is ultimately the best friend of innovators in Washington.

If anybody could make the decision about technology in DC, I'd want it to be President Trump. Not cabinet secretaries, not the White House staff, not members of Congress, not senators, not think tanks, I would really want every decision, if he had the time, to be made by President Trump because his instincts on this are really good.

He wants America to win. He does not believe in unnecessary regulation. He doesn't have all these doomer anxieties. He listens to a broad cross-section of people. I mean, he talks to all the CEOs. He is very up to speed on all these issues.

And I spoke to this at the G20 this past week. There are great deals for local communities to be had. This is the point that I think needs to be made, the reason why local communities should embrace this is not because of some abstract concern about innovation.

They should do it when the deal is good for them, and there are good deals to be had.

We've seen that in Loudoun County, Virginia, property taxes went down by $6,000 because they're getting all this data center revenue. In Louisiana, there's a county that was able to give teachers their first bonus in years because of data center revenue.

So we're starting to see all these examples where if you make the right deal, it will lower your electricity costs because they will stand up net new power generation, they will pay for grid upgrades. It does not use an excessive amount of water, that's total fake news. We know the systems recirculate. And these data centers can be put in places where they're not bothering people.

So there is a good deal to be made there and ultimately, just one last point on this, President Trump supports local choice on this. I'm seeing all this fake news, you know, Democrats saying that the administration's trying to shove these data centers down the throats of local communities.

Not true. In the policy document that I worked on, we expressly said that data centers remain a state and local decision. So no one is forcing these local communities, but what the president is saying is, ‘Don't believe this media disinformation campaign. It can be a good deal for you if you're willing to embrace it.’”

- The return of the "debasement trade" acted as a catalyst for $BTC which pumped from $64k to $80k in 3 days. This revived the crypto market and has questioned whether we're out of the bear market or not.

- $ZEC has been unstoppable and pumped from $500 to $1200.

- $PUMP had a massive run and went from $2bn to $5.5bn FDV at its top

- $ENA had a +120% move in 4 days and announced that they would be conducting buybacks

- $HYPE reached a new ATH at almost $90. $LIT pumped from $2 to almost $5.

- $XRP squeezed surprisingly strongly from $1 to $1.7 at the top of the spike

- 3 main scam coins: $TUT (30x then died), $AKE (200x bottom to top in 2 months), $BTW (12x)

- $CHIP is up 3x from its bottom after 4 months of bleeding
